plan.stage: L5-02 shared simulation/verification pool and producer-owned lifetime
plan.policy: baseline: per-slot TRUNCATE; candidate: per-slot PASSIVE unless WAL>=8MiB, then TRUNCATE; final TRUNCATE before Store.close. Same NORMAL synchronous and 1000-page auto-checkpoint; no deferred durability checkpoint.
plan.decisionRule: Retain current runtime unless consistent paired end-to-end benefit is demonstrated with unchanged outputs, durability and capacity. Native checkpoint savings alone are insufficient. No production change from this observer experiment.

outputEncoding: Each record.outputsRef resolves to its exact normalized outputs array in outputSets. Keys are SHA256 of UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys and comma/colon separators. Identical arrays are stored once; all measured values and original record file digests remain per trial.
interpretation: Decision: retain the production per-slot TRUNCATE policy; this is a measurement-only change. No consistent end-to-end speedup is established by this bounded local pilot.
Wall medians 42534.310 -> 42401.369 ms (-0.31%). All five paired differences are retained, including slower candidate trials.

Both variants use exactly the same clean runtime source. The candidate changes only the experiment process via an explicit observer adapter around the existing per-slot SQLite pragma and Store close, not a shipped runtime option. Source SHA alone does not describe the candidate; pair it with observerSha256 and policy.

Both use the actual Store settings: WAL, synchronous NORMAL (1), 4096-byte pages and 1000-page auto-checkpoint. The setting is sampled after the real Store migrations; querying immediately after creating an empty database can transiently show FULL (2). No synchronous or auto-checkpoint assignment is made by the observer.

Candidate preserves a checkpoint after every published slot: PASSIVE while physical WAL bytes are below 8MiB; TRUNCATE at or above the threshold; a final TRUNCATE before close is included in measured wall/process CPU. Reject busy or incomplete checkpoints in this isolated producer. No checkpoint is deferred under NORMAL, and no OFF/NORMAL change is used as a performance optimization.

All 12 trials have ten fresh matches, identical normalized slot/result/compressed chunk/checkpoint hashes, reuse 0, complete validation 30 times (10 main plus 20 shared Worker), no incomplete spans or dropped records. The two-admission/40MiB queue and all existing byte/privacy/durability checks remain.

The 8MiB threshold was never reached by these ten-match trials; that branch is exercised only by a separate synthetic 9MiB metadata probe. This does not prove all-match worst-case capacity or behavior with long-lived concurrent readers. DB/WAL/SHM and Worker memory are sampled maxima, final directory sizes are not peak disk use.

walNativeInclusiveMedianMs includes only actual explicit SQLite checkpoint calls (candidate final included), excluding observer stat/assertion overhead and internal auto/close checkpoints. walCheckpointInclusiveMedianMs includes the observer at the original per-slot span; final is reported separately. Full wall/process CPU include all checkpoints and Store close. Process CPU includes all Workers; inclusive spans overlap and cannot be summed.

Separate process-exit probes stop after durable publication at the third slot immediately before/after its checkpoint, skip close/finally, reopen SQLite, verify quick_check and unchanged result/job/attempt rows, and resume through actual batch replay validation with cached results and no extra attempts. These are application crashes, not power-loss/system-crash tests and do not upgrade NORMAL durability guarantees.

Checkpoint frequency under NORMAL is part of the durability boundary. A pure size/count-based deferral is not equivalent to this candidate and is not adopted or claimed safe by these process-exit tests. The SQLite documentation distinguishes application crashes from power-loss durability.

Same two characters, five official fields, both placements and one seed, unchanged 6000-step rules/budget. Startup, planning, output comparison, GitHub runner setup/artifacts/waits, R2/Pages and all-7600 acceptance are excluded. No scaling, end-to-end 270/300-second, runner-count or production storage performance claim follows.

The registered plan retains its inherited stage label describing the shared-pool baseline; the explicit policy field and this report stage identify the WAL experiment. No trials were removed or relabeled.

reproduction.instructions: Use a clean checkout of plan.baseline (same as candidate) with the pinned frozen install. Extract the prior report base driver and this report reproduction.files to an ignored scratch directory; verify their hashes. Adapt only runner workspace paths. Preserve the registered order and finite 120-second per-trial timeout. Invoke node --import tsx l5-wal-pilot.mjs REPOSITORY OUTPUT VARIANT from apps/cli; run crash probes separately via node --import apps/cli/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs l5-wal-crash.mjs REPOSITORY OUTPUT. Do not edit tracked files or run tests/other simulations concurrently. All original receipts/logs/digests are retained.
